html:
Roman emperor from 161 to 180 and a Stoic philosopher. He was adopted into the ruling house at Hadrian's wish and ruled at first jointly with Lucius Verus, the first time Rome had two emperors at once.

He is remembered as the last of the "Five Good Emperors", but his reign was hard:

  • A war with Parthia from 161 to 166 brought back the Antonine Plague, which ran through the empire for years.
  • From 166 the Marcomannic Wars kept him on the Danube frontier for most of his last decade.
  • On campaign he wrote the private notes now called the Meditations.

His doctor was Galen. He died in 180, probably at Vindobona (Vienna) or Sirmium, and was followed by his son Commodus, whose bad rule is often taken as the end of Rome's best age. His bronze statue on horseback survives in Rome, perhaps because later Christians took it for Constantine.
sum: Roman emperor from 161 to 180 and a Stoic philosopher. He was adopted into the ruling house at Hadrian's wish and ruled at first jointly with Lucius Verus, the first time Rome had two emperors at once.
